Hi Jordan / Priya,

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery:

- BrightPath needs assurance that any patient PII included in prompts is not used for model training and is stored only in permitted locations.
- Data residency: US-only (must stay in us-east region).
- Retention: short-term debugging logs OK; production logs and prompts/outputs should be retained no longer than 30 days unless otherwise agreed.
- Logging & audit: we need request/response audit logs for 90 days for compliance reviews.
- KV cache / internal model caches: we need confirmation these are not persisted to long-term storage or re-used across tenants.

I've attached a short summary and our standard PII handling overview (redwood-pii-handling-summary.pdf). I'll loop in Neha (security) and Marissa (solutions) to provide the technical confirmation and any SOC2 artifacts.

Can you confirm the items above and any additional constraints we should account for in the mutual action plan?

Next step: Neha will confirm retention and residency specifics; Marissa will scope implementation steps. If acceptable, we can put a draft MSA amendment for data handling on the table.

Hi Jordan / team — thanks for the clear questions. Below are the confirmed details from a security/compliance perspective for Redwood (hosted offering). I included the short answers first, then the technical clarifications. SOC2 summary attached (SOC2-summary.pdf) and link to our compliance page: https://redwood.example.com/soc2

Short answers (explicit):
- Model training: Redwood does NOT use customer prompts or outputs to train or improve open-source model weights. Customer data is not fed into public model training pipelines.
- Retention: By default, hosted requests (request/response bodies including prompts and outputs) are retained for 30 days for debugging, abuse detection, and operational troubleshooting. Customers can request shorter retention or opt into a "no-retention" mode via contract for hosted (we offer Dedicated/Private for strict non-retention).
- Embeddings: Embeddings generated via our API are treated like other outputs — by default retained 30 days. If you persist embeddings in your own storage (e.g., via our SDK), Redwood does not automatically copy those back into our logs.
- Logs/audit: Request metadata and audit logs (request id, timestamp, requester, route, model used) are retained for 90 days. Audit logs do not include full cache contents.
- KV cache / model caches: KV caches are ephemeral in-memory structures tied to live inference instances and are not persisted to long-term storage or reused across tenants. We do NOT persist KV cache contents to disk in hosted production; they are not included in logs.
- Data residency: For hosted US-region accounts, all data-at-rest and backups are stored in our US regions (us-east) and encrypted at rest. We can provide residual handling commitments in the contract. For Dedicated/Private, residency can be configured to your VPC/region.
- Encryption & keys: Data at rest is encrypted using server-side KMS (managed by Redwood) for hosted customers. We support customer-managed keys (BYOK) for Dedicated and Private offerings.
- Access controls: Only authorized operations and a small security/ops on-call team can access raw request data for emergency debugging; access is audited and requires approval.

Technical clarifications / notes:
1) "Default retention" refers to our standard hosted product. If BrightPath requires a contract-level guarantee of zero retention of request/response bodies, we recommend Dedicated or a Private deployment; we can also add a contractual data retention term for hosted, but there are operational trade-offs (reduced debugging visibility).
2) Embeddings: If you plan to persist embeddings in BrightPath-managed storage, Redwood will not store copies beyond the standard retention window unless features like persistent index are enabled. If you want a workflow with no copies retained at Redwood, we can configure that at contract stage.
3) KV cache: short lived, in-memory only. No long-term persistence, not surfaced to logs.
4) SOC2: attaching a redacted summary and our auditor contact. For complete artifacts (attestation letter, full report) we can execute an NDA and provide to your GRC team.

Attachments: SOC2-summary.pdf (summary), redwood-pii-handling-summary.pdf (overview).

Next steps:
- If these defaults work, Rishi / Marissa, please capture the 30-day retention + 90-day audit log window in the mutual action plan.
- If BrightPath needs no-retention, please indicate and we'll scope Dedicated/Private pricing and contractual language.
- Jordan: happy to do a 20-minute call to walk your GRC through the details — propose Thu 8/19 10:00am PT if that works.
